id.description:
UUID v4 minted by the caller; the idempotency key. An audited request's id stays
deduplicated for as long as its audit row is kept (`audit.retention_days`, BUS.md §5.3).

payload.description: Op-specific; `{}` when the op takes nothing.

token.description: Session token binding an `agent:<name>` actor on the socket door.

Actor.description: "user" | "agent:<session-name>" | "test" | "system". "system" is the engine itself: it appears on events, audit rows and holds, and every door rejects a request that claims it

id.description: `null` only when the request could not be parsed far enough to read one (`bus.parse`).

replayed.description: Present (true) when the id was seen before and the recorded result was returned.

mail.description: Live, unaudited sideband. Present only when an authenticated agent has priority mail.

Response.description: A response envelope (BUS.md §1.2). Exactly one of `result` / `error` is present.

message.description: Human sentence; may change; never parse it.

Confirm.description: The op that lifts a hold (present iff `kind == held`).

priority.description: Number of unread priority messages for the authenticated agent session.

cause.description: Request id that caused it; absent for system-originated events.

Event.description: A fact about a mutation that already happened (BUS.md §1.3).

stream.description:
`pty` | `logcat` | `mirror`, all on the socket door (BUS.md §7). `app.log.tail` declares
a `log` stream but is not built: it sends no frames.

mirror_id.description: `mirror` only: which `device.mirror.start` this frame belongs to.

epoch.description: `pty` only: increments on every spawn/wake; `seq` restarts at 0 within it.

data.description:
base64 for `pty`; a line for `logcat`; for `mirror`, a base64 video packet or a status
object (state, picture size, device, and the typed reason on the last one).

Frame.description: A data-plane frame (BUS.md §7) as carried on the socket door.

implemented.description: Whether the running engine has a handler for it (else `bus.not_implemented`).

call.description:
All-layers verdict for the asking actor. `None` when nothing evaluated it (the static
schema render), so a reader never mistakes "not computed" for "callable".

why.description: Which layer decided `call`, in one phrase.

oneOf.description: `user` and `test` (and `system`).
Everyone may call it, but the op exists *for* agents (self-report style).

Doors.description:
Which doors carry an op. A `socket_only` op acts on the connection that sends it (a
subscriber, a wait), so the socket door answers it; the engine refuses it with `bus.door`.

oneOf.description: Callable as asked.
Refused before the handler runs.
Callable, but only for the actor's own session (or its PAIR partner, for reads).

Callable.description:
Whether the asking actor may really call an op, across all three gating layers
(registry `actors`, runtime row scope, and the role allowlist). `bus.ops` reports it.

can_call.description: Every op this actor may really call, all three gating layers applied.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots this actor may write to, worktree first.

events.description: Exact names or `prefix.*`. Empty waits for anything.

timeout_ms.description: How long to block before giving up. Default 60s, clamped to an hour.

matching.description:
Only an event whose payload has every one of these top-level keys equal to the value
given, e.g. `{"request_id": 7}`. Omit to take the first event that matches by name.
Anything but an object is `bus.schema`: read as "no filter", it woke on any event.

spawn_profile.description: How Relay spawns it: flags, env, hook file layout. Opaque, for display and diagnosis.

guarded.description:
Whether this provider supports Relay's `PreToolUse` guardrail and lifecycle adapters.
Provider-native trust may still require one explicit approval before a generated hook runs.

payload.description: `null` when the payload was larger than 64 KiB.

expect.description: `{updated_at}` of the entity after the op; `audit.undo` refuses on mismatch (§5.5).

orders.description: Every workspace whose `order` changes, each once. The rest keep theirs.

force.description:
Also remove every project in it, closing their open sessions (`project.remove` with `force`).
Without it the op refuses `workspace.has_projects`.

remove_worktrees.description:
With `force`: also delete the Relay-pool worktrees of the sessions it closes. Branches
are always kept; off by default, so every checkout stays on disk.

discard_changes.description:
With `remove_worktrees`: delete them even with uncommitted changes. Without it, a dirty
one is refused `worktree.dirty` before anything is closed or removed (RA-405).

orders.description: Every project whose `order` changes, each once. The rest keep theirs.

force.description:
Close its open sessions (`session.close`, worktree kept) and stop its device runs first.
Without it the op refuses `project.sessions_live` / `project.activity_live`.

remove_worktrees.description:
With `force`: also delete the Relay-pool worktrees of the sessions it closes. Branches
are always kept; off by default, so every checkout stays on disk.

discard_changes.description:
With `remove_worktrees`: delete them even with uncommitted changes. Without it, a dirty
one is refused `worktree.dirty` before anything is closed or removed (RA-405).

path.description:
The repository's new root: absolute, a git repository, no other project's path, and inside
a workspace (the project moves to the innermost one that contains it).

backup_path.description: The backup to pass to `project.restore`: the newest one that still holds the project.

A file in the store's `backups/` directory, as `project.removed.list` or the removal's
`project.deleted` event names it.

parent_id.description: Create it straight as a sub-task of this one; refused past `TASK_DEPTH_MAX`.

labels.description: Free-form tags; unknown names are created in the project's label set.

note_id.description: The note this task is made from: a live note in the same project, or `notes.not_found`.

TaskState.description: Agent lifecycle on a task, independent of column (BUS.md §11.1, confirmed 2026-08-17).

TaskType.description:
A first-class classification, separate from the free-form `labels` (BUS.md §11.1).
`Task` is the neutral default and is what every pre-v16 row migrated to; the other four
are the vocabulary the board filters on.

module_name.description:
The name of `module_id`'s module, completed (archived) ones included, so a card can be
labelled without a `module.list` (RA-495). Absent from an older engine.

parent_id.description: Parent task, if this is a sub-task. Nesting is capped at [`TASK_DEPTH_MAX`] levels.

depth.description: 0 for a root task, 1 for its child, and so on — never above `TASK_DEPTH_MAX - 1`.

children.description: Direct children, in board order. Children stay real tasks with their own cards.

rollup.description: Progress over the whole subtree, for the parent's `n/m done` badge.

labels.description: Free-form tags, sorted; the supplementary layer under `type`.

blocked_by.description: Tasks this one waits on (stored edges).

blocks.description: Tasks waiting on this one (the inverse read of `blocked_by`).

duplicate_of.description: The task this duplicates, if any.

note_id.description:
The note this task was made from, if any (`task.create` with `note_id`). Cleared when
that note is purged; absent from an older engine.

sessions.description: Every session ever dispatched to it, in order; a PAIR adds two.

TaskRollup.description:
Roll-up of a parent's descendants (BUS.md §11.1). Counts the whole subtree, not just the
direct children, so a grandparent reads as one body of work. Zero `total` = a leaf.

path.description: Path under the store's attachment dir.

comments.description:
Every comment on the task, oldest first; not paged. `task.comment` rows stay out of
`history`, so a comment is reported once.

TaskComment.description:
One entry in a task's discussion, GitHub-issue style. `author` is the session name for an
agent and `user` for a person, as `mailbox.send` renders `from`.

label.description: One label name, exact and case-insensitive.

session.description: A session name; matches every task that session was ever dispatched to.

note_id.description: Only the tasks made from this note.

parent_id.description: `Some(Some(id))` = children of that task, `Some(None)` = roots only, absent = every task.

limit.description:
Page size, default 1000, at most 2000. Done cards sort last, so a page cut short drops
the oldest finished work first.

offset.description: Skip this many tasks of the ordered result: the previous page's `next_offset`.

summary.description: Leave each task's `body` and `changelog` empty: a board needs titles, not essays.

next_offset.description: Set when more tasks match than this page holds: pass it as `offset`.

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

parent_id.description: Absent or null detaches the task back to a root.

Label.description: A free-form supplementary tag, scoped to a project. Types classify; labels annotate.

TaskRelation.description:
Task-to-task edges other than parent/child (BUS.md §11.1). Only these two are stored;
`blocks` is the inverse read of `blocked_by` and never has a row of its own.

fanout.description: Also dispatch every not-done descendant, one fresh session each. Requires `create`.

start.description:
Defaults to true. False stages the assignment without starting the provider, so a
multi-task launch can attach its complete queue before the first agent turn.

worktree.description: `"new"` (default: pooled worktree), `"primary"`, or an absolute path of an existing worktree.

use_api_key.description: Claude only: run on the API key the key proxy holds instead of the signed-in account.

prompt.description: Persist the initial assignment before spawning, so a partial launch can recover it.

intent.description: One line of what this session is doing, in its own words (`session.intent`).

use_api_key.description:
Claude runs on an API key instead of the signed-in account, through the key proxy, which
holds the key as its own system user (docs/KEY-PROXY.md). Relay never has the key.

column.description: The column the task goes back to; not `done`.

position.description: Its 0-based index in that column, as in `task.move`.

state.description: The run state it had before the approval.

sha.description:
The commit link the approval created, removed again. Absent when the approval linked a
commit that was already there, which then stays.

project_id.description:
Required from the person; an agent may leave it out for its own project, the only one
it may name (D106).

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

group_by.description: Only `"priority"`, the default; anything else is refused.

include_deleted.description: Also list soft-deleted notes (`deleted_at` set), which `notes.restore` brings back.

summary.description: Cut each `body` to a preview of its first 240 characters; `notes.get` has the whole note.

expected.description: Original editable field values; every supplied value must still match atomically.

expected_updated_at.description:
The target note's `updated_at` as you last read it. When given and the note has changed
since, nothing is appended (`notes.edit_conflict`); omitted, the text is appended as before.

delivery.description:
`queued` (at least one addressee is live), `session_parked` (all parked),
`not_running` (all created or exited), or `no_recipients` (an empty broadcast).

state.description:
The recipient session's state right now: `running` will see it, `parked` will not
until it wakes.

before.description: Only messages older than this message id: the previous page's `next_before`.

messages.description: Oldest first. Without `unread_only` this is the newest page; with it, the oldest unread.

next_before.description: Set when older messages remain: pass it as `before` for the page before this one.

more_unread.description: More unread messages remain past this page (`unread_only`): ack these, then ask again.

prompt.description: Omitted preserves the allocated assignment; an empty string explicitly clears it.

discard_changes.description:
Delete the worktree even with uncommitted changes (tracked edits or untracked files).
Without it, removing a dirty Relay-pool worktree is refused `worktree.dirty` (RA-405).

status.description:
`completed` (default), `blocked`, or `partial`. An op that can only report success
gets reported success (D118).

text.description: One line, present tense. Empty clears it.

paths.description: Worktree-relative paths this session is taking on.

symbol.description: Narrow the claim to one symbol within each path.

exclusive.description:
Refuse the whole claim if any path is already claimed by a peer, instead of recording
it alongside theirs and reporting the collision.

collisions.description: Peers already holding one of these paths. Empty is the quiet, expected case.

paths.description: Omit to release every claim this session holds.

intent.description:
One line of what this peer is doing, in its own words (`session.intent`). Coordination
needs to know what a peer is *up to*, which no amount of state and branch names says.

text.description: Everything, skills included. What the UI shows.

compact.description:
State, peers and adjacent work only — the part small enough to inject on every
spawn. Skill bodies are referenced by path instead of inlined (D101).

task.description: Current task retained for older clients and one-task agents.

tasks.description: Current task followed by every queued or in-review task attached to this session.

assignment.description:
The launch prompt, on the session's first launch only: a relaunch may come long after
that work was done (RA-397). The brief keeps it as the original launch assignment.

brief_path.description: Worktree-relative path of the full brief.

peers.description: Everyone else live in this project, now.

can_call.description: Every op this session may really call, all three gating layers applied.

discovery.description: How to inspect operation summaries and exact payload/result schemas without guessing.

comms.description: How to reach the peers above, and which channel actually reaches all of them.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots this session may write to, worktree first.

dry_run.description: The op that answers "would this be allowed?" without doing it.

exceptions.description:
What to do when a refusal stands between you and the task: how to ask the user for an
exception and wait for the answer.

until_detach.description:
Borrow the size: on a connection door, the PTY goes back to the size it had when this
connection detaches from the session or goes away, unless someone resized it since.

cols.description: The live PTY's size; absent when the text comes from a saved scrollback.

after.description:
The `cursor` of the previous answer: only what the agent wrote since. Absent, the
conversation's last `limit` messages.

limit.description: At most this many messages, the newest kept (default 200, at most 1000).

cursor.description: Pass it back as `after` for what comes next.

reset.description:
The messages replace everything read before: the conversation moved to another file
(a resume, a new conversation) or `after` was past its end.

found.description: Whether the provider's conversation was found; false before its first hook names it.

id.description: Stable across reads: the provider's own id for the record, or its byte offset.

role.description:
`user`, `assistant` (`blocks` of `text` and `tool_use {id, name, summary}`), or `tool`
(`{tool_use_id, is_error, text}`) — a thread message's shape (`thread.get`).

bytes_b64.description:
A PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP picture, base64 (at most 4 MiB decoded): a photo or a
screenshot from the phone for the agent to look at.

path.description:
Where it was written, from the session's checkout: `.relay/attachments/<name>`, which
git never sees. A message naming this path shows the agent the picture.

project_id.description:
Only this project's sessions. Each one costs a `git status` of its worktree, so a
client describing one project's panes should not pay for every project's (RA-235).

discard_changes.description:
Delete the worktree even with uncommitted changes. Without it, a dirty Relay-pool
worktree that the discard would delete is refused `worktree.dirty` (RA-405).

url.description: Anything `git clone` takes: an https or ssh URL, or `owner/name` for a GitHub repository.

name.description: The folder name under `.relay/linked/`; the repository's name when omitted.

branch.description: Check out this branch instead of the remote's default.

name.description: The folder under `.relay/linked/`, which names it to `session.repo.remove`.

url.description: Its `origin` remote; absent when it has none.

branch.description: The branch checked out; absent on a detached HEAD.

unpushed.description:
What removing it would lose; absent when nothing would be. `session.repo.add` does not
look: it has just cloned it.

changed.description: Entries `git status` lists, untracked files included; `None` when the scan failed.

commits.description:
Commits on a branch (or a detached HEAD) that no remote-tracking ref contains, as of the
clone's last fetch; `None` when git could not tell.

branches.description: The local branches holding those commits.

ignored.description: Git-ignored files nothing could bring back: an `.env`, a keystore, a local database.

discard_changes.description:
Delete it even with uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, stashes or ignored keepers.
Without it, such a repository is refused `session.repo_unpushed` and kept.

verdict.description:
Always `allow`. A refusal arrives as a typed `refused` error and a hold as a typed `held`
error whose `confirm` names the hold, never as a verdict here (BUS.md §9.3).

error.description: Never set; a refusal is the response's `error`.

hold_id.description: Never set; a hold's id is in the `held` error's `confirm.payload`.

full.description:
Return every string whole, however large. By default a string over 64 KiB in the
payload or details is cut to its first 4 KiB and named in `elided`.

request.description:
The exact frozen action, with authentication material removed. `guardrail.confirm`
replays the stored action whole, whatever was elided here.

elided.description: JSON pointers (`/request/payload/new_text`, `/hold/details/reason`) of the strings cut short.

scope.description: Exception requests only: how long the grant lasts. Defaults to what the agent asked for.

GrantScope.description: How long an approved exception lasts: one use, or until the session ends.

workspace_id.description: One of the two, or neither for the global layer.

denied_commands.description:
Command patterns refused for `kind: exec`. Matched against the *parsed argv* of each
command in the line, never as a raw substring, so quoted data mentioning one is fine.

allowed_write_roots.description:
Absolute roots an agent may write to outside its worktree — scratch space, which is
not a repo-integrity concern. `$TMPDIR` is always honoured in addition to these.

agent_builds.description:
Whether an agent's `integration.request` may run the project's build command without a
person confirming it. Off by default: the build runs outside any sandbox (RA-167), so an
agent's request that builds is held for confirmation; a merge-only request is not.

check_on_push.description:
Whether an agent's `git push` first runs the project's check — its `build_cmd`, else
the test command of the build tool at the checkout's root — and is refused when the
check fails. On by default. A person's own push never runs it, so pushing a branch does
not execute what that branch's code does.

GuardrailConfig.description: Effective guardrail configuration after global + project merge.

min_file_lines.description:
The percentage rule is skipped for files shorter than this. A percentage of a very
short file measures nothing: one line of a one-line file is 100%.

allow_if_recoverable.description:
Let a large rewrite through when git can put the file back — committed and unmodified,
or ignored entirely. Set false to hold on volume alone.

DestructiveWrite.description: A write is destructive when either threshold is exceeded.

ShapeGate.description: A built-in validator attached to one critical, worktree-relative path.

RoleAllowlist.description: Role allow-sets are configurable, but the defaults are the baseline in BUS.md §9.1.

workspace_id.description: Patch this workspace's layer. At most one of `workspace_id` / `project_id`.

patch.description: Merged into the layer's stored overrides; `null` clears a key back to the inherited value.

workspace_id.description: At most one of the two; neither reads the global layer.

inherited.description: What this layer would get with no overrides of its own: the parent layer's effective config.

overrides.description: This layer's stored overrides, exactly as stored.

sources.description: Leaf path (`caps.files`, `protected_paths`) to the layer that decided its value.

GuardrailLayer.description:
Which layer of guardrail configuration a value lives in. Each layer overrides the one
before it: defaults, then global, then the project's workspace, then the project.

paths.description: Worktree-relative paths the plan intends to touch.

lines.description: Lines the plan expects to change in total, if known.

commands.description: Commands the plan intends to run.

verdict.description: The worst verdict across everything below.

files.description: What the plan costs against the commit caps.

write_roots.description: Absolute roots the caller may write to.

policy.description: The policy that decided it, when one did.

kind.description:
`command` for a denied command, `path` for a protected path / write root / large rewrite,
`cap` for the commit caps.

value.description: The exact command line; the path (worktree-relative or absolute); or `files=N lines=M`.

reason.description: Why you cannot progress without it. The user reads this before deciding.

scope.description: What you are asking for; the user may grant less. Default `once`.

ExceptionKind.description:
What an agent asks to be let past. `command` lifts a denied command, `path` a protected
path, a write root or a destructive-write rule, `cap` the commit caps.

created.description: False when an identical request from this session was already open.

wait_for.description: The event announcing the answer; wait with `bus.wait {events:[wait_for], matching:{request_id}}`.

id.description:
Also the id of the hold that carries it, so `guardrail.confirm` / `guardrail.reject`
answer it with `hold_id` set to this.

value.description:
The exact command, the path (worktree-relative, a glob, or an absolute root), or the
caps wanted (`files=N lines=M`; empty lifts the caps for the grant's life).

active.description: Approved, not revoked, and (for `once`) not yet used.

GuardrailException.description: An agent's request to be let past one guardrail, and — once a person answered — the grant.

oneOf.description: Waiting for an answer.
Approved and still usable.

discard_changes.description:
Delete the worktree even with uncommitted changes or git-ignored files worth keeping.
Without it, removing a dirty worktree is refused `worktree.dirty`, as `session.close` is.

rescued.description:
The ref (`refs/relay/rescue/...`) now holding the commits of a detached HEAD that no
branch or tag contained; absent when there were none.

base.description:
What the counts are against: the base's remote-tracking branch (`origin/main`) or the local
base, whichever is further ahead; the remote one when they have diverged.

behind.description: Commits on `base` this checkout's HEAD does not have: what a rebase onto it would bring in.

ahead.description: Commits on this checkout's HEAD that `base` does not have.

files.description:
A wholly untracked directory is one entry, its path ending in `/`. At most a few thousand
entries: conflicts first, then other tracked changes, then untracked ones.

truncated.description: Whether `files` stops short of every change git reported.

total.description: How many entries git reported, `files` included; more than `files.len()` when truncated.

staged.description: Compare with the index, what a commit would record, instead of the working tree.

old_path.description: For a rename, the file's path in the old side (`renamed_from` in `git.status`).

branch.description: The branch name on the remote, `feature`.

local.description: The local branch of the same name, if there is one; switching to the remote selects it.

name.description:
A local branch, or a remote-tracking one (`origin/feature`) to check out as a new local
tracking branch.

carry_changes.description:
Bring uncommitted changes to tracked files along, as `git switch` does. Git still refuses
when the target branch would overwrite them; nothing is ever discarded.

branch.description: The local branch now checked out.

created.description: Whether a local tracking branch was created for a remote branch.

refresh.description:
Ask GitHub now instead of answering from the last listing (kept up to a minute, and
dropped by `git.push` and `git.pr.open`). For an explicit refresh, not for every redraw.

failed.description:
Branches found merged that were not deleted (or, on a dry run, would not be), with why:
a dirty or still-held checkout, a rebase in progress, a failed delete (RA-373).

session.description: The closed session that worked on it.

reason.description: Why: how the work was found merged, or what unmerged work kept it.

merged.description: Its work was found merged; a `kept` row with this set is one cleanup could not delete.

limit.description: Most entries listed per directory, default 2000, at most 5000.

truncated.description:
Directories cut short at `limit`, by worktree-relative path, with how many entries each
really holds. Ask for one again with its `path` and a larger `limit` to see more.

worktree.description:
The checkout to put it back into (`@project` or a worktree path). Default: the one it was
deleted from, or the project's primary checkout once that one is gone.
The checkout it was put back into.

fallback.description:
Set when no `worktree` was named and the one it was deleted from is gone, so it went to
the project's primary checkout instead.

worktree.description: The checkout it was deleted from, and where `file.restore` puts it back by default.

available.description: Whether the trashed bytes are still on disk.

glob.description:
A glob without `/` (`*.rs`) matches the file name at any depth; one with `/`, or a
leading `/` to anchor it, matches the whole worktree-relative path.

col.description: 1-based byte offset of the match in the whole line.

text.description: The line, or for a long one a window of it around the match.

text_offset.description:
Set when `text` is a window: the byte offset in the line where it starts, so the match
begins `col - 1 - text_offset` bytes into `text`.

lease.description:
Who is using this device right now, if anyone. A conflicting run, install or claim
from anyone else is refused with `device.busy` until it is released.

device.description:
The device serial, or `*` when the command named no device (adb's only device, or
Gradle's every device): that lease conflicts with every device.

session.description: The holding session's name; `None` when the user holds it directly.

action.description:
What the holder is doing, in a few words (`device.run debug from relay/brisk-otter`,
`adb install app-debug.apk`).

expires_in_s.description: Seconds until the lease lapses on its own; `None` while it lasts as long as its run.

DeviceLease.description:
One holder's exclusive use of an Android device: a `device.run` in flight, an agent's
`adb install` / `gradlew install*` seen by the guardrail hook, or an explicit `device.claim`.
Released with a `device.lease.released` event, so `bus.wait` can wait for it.

kind.description:
`run` installs and launches on `device`; `build` produces an artifact and
leaves `device` empty (D152).

artifact.description: Absolute path of the APK / AAB a finished `build` produced.

variant.description: Gradle variant and artifact format for a release build; absent for device runs.

publish.description: True when this build was also handed to Gradle Play Publisher.

signing.description: `signed`, `unsigned`, or `unverified` after Relay inspects the artifact.

device.description: Serial from `device.list`; omit to claim every device (what a bare `adb` would touch).

action.description: What you will be doing, shown to anyone refused with `device.busy`.

minutes.description: How long to hold it. Default 10, at most 60; released early by `device.release`.

device.description: Serial to release; omit to release every lease you hold.

windows.description: Provider's own units and windows, opaque; the UI knows each provider's shape.

summary.description:
Cut each body to its opening, frontmatter included, instead of the whole SKILL.md;
`skill.get` returns one whole body.

description.description:
What the skill is for: the `description` of its SKILL.md front matter, else the first
line of prose after it; empty when there is neither. Read from the whole body, so it is
there even when `skill.list {summary: true}` cuts the body short.

source_ref.description:
The branch or tag a GitHub skill was installed from; `None` is the repository's
default branch (or a local skill). A refresh pulls this ref again.

Branch or tag to clone; overrides one named by a `tree/<ref>` URL. When neither names
one and `subdir` is an installed skill's `source_path`, its recorded `source_ref` is
kept, so "Update from GitHub" stays on the branch the skill came from.

replace_skill_id.description:
Explicit permission to replace one visible skill when its name conflicts with the
downloaded SKILL.md. Hidden soft-deleted rows are reclaimed automatically.

docs.description: Documentation files, relative to the plugin root; `plugin.get` returns their text.

enabled_in.description: Projects the plugin is switched on for.

suggested_for.description:
Projects whose checkout looks like this plugin's kind of project (for Unreal Engine, a
`.uproject` at the root) and that do not have it on yet.

Plugin.description:
A plugin bundled with Relay: skills, always-on agent instructions, documentation and MCP
servers that reach every agent of a project the plugin is switched on for (D159).

name.description: The skill's folder name, which is also its provider-visible name.

files.description: Files in the skill folder, `SKILL.md` included.

instructions.description: The instructions every agent of an enabled project receives in its brief.

count_only.description: Only `unread`: no rows are read and `notifications` comes back empty. For a badge.

unread.description:
Unread notifications matching `project_id` / `category`, however many `limit` and
`unread_only` leave out of `notifications` (RA-490). Absent from an older engine.

link.description: Deep link: an op to run when clicked.

PaneTarget.description: What a pane shows; shape depends on `PaneKind`.

today.description: The day to read the month from; today in the engine's time zone when absent.

empty.description: No accounts and no entries: draw the honest empty state.

recent.description:
The latest few entries, for Home. Left out for a model, which answered "the biggest expense"
from these few instead of the period's entries.

expected.description: What an even spend would have used by the end of today.

pace_delta.description: Positive when spending runs faster than an even pace.

days_left.description: Days still to spend in, today included.

daily_allowance.description: What can go out each remaining day and still land on budget. Zero once the budget is gone.

spent_fraction.description: Spent as a fraction of the budget; may exceed 1. Zero without a budget.

pace_fraction.description: Where the pace tick sits on the meter, 0..1.

left.description: What is still to spend: `budget` less `spent`, below zero once it is over budget.

pace_delta.description: Above zero when spending runs ahead of an even pace through the period.

line.description: Where it stands in words, to the cent: "$87.60 over pace, $118.85 left", "$7.99 over budget".

registration.description: An investment account's tax wrapper; `None` on every other account.

AccountType.description:
`Investment` holds money put to work (a TFSA, an RRSP, a brokerage account); its value can be
updated by hand.

Registration.description:
How the tax rules see an `Investment` account (docs/INVESTMENTS.md). A field of the account,
not an account type of its own.

GoalKind.description:
What a goal measures.

- `Savings`: a pot filled by contributions, toward a target and an optional date.
- `Balance`: an account (or everything you own, net of what you owe) reaching an amount by a date.
- `Invest`: each month, money moved into investment accounts: a share of what came in, or a set amount.
- `Save`: each month, what is kept of what came in: a share of it, or a set amount.

MoneyTx.description: One entry as a client draws it, its account and category names joined in.

net_worth.description: Every unarchived account's balance added up, as money.summary's `net_worth`.

devices.description: Phones that sync with this ledger, the latest first.

period_offset.description: 0 is the current budget period, -1 the one before.

query.description: Matches the note, category or account in any case and alphabet.

periods.description: How many budget periods, ending with `period_offset`'s: 1 to 6 (24 by period). Default 1.

period_offset.description: The last period: 0 is the current one, -1 the one before.

category.description: Only this category, by name (any case).

cumulative.description: Running totals across weeks or days, for pace.

today.description: The day to read the current period from; today in the engine's time zone when absent.

MoneySeriesIn.description:
The question a chart asks. A chart keeps this, not its numbers, so it redraws when the ledger
moves.

oneOf.description: Income less spending.
One label per category, the largest first; each period is a series.
Week 1 is the period's first seven days; each period is a series.
Day 1 is the period's first day; each period is a series.
One label per budget period, oldest first; one series.

label_colors.description: Each label's category colour (Tally's palette index), when the labels are categories.

values.description: One value per label, minor units.

known.description:
By week or day, in the period still running: how many labels it has reached. Later ones
have not happened yet, so a running total stops here instead of going flat.

to_account_id.description: Transfers only: the account the money goes to.

previous.description:
The entry as it was before this change: a card shows before → after, and its Undo puts
it back.

MoneyTxChanged.description: One entry as a client draws it, its account and category names joined in.

amount.description: Zero or less removes the budget.

registration.description: Investment accounts only: TFSA, RRSP, FHSA…

institution.description: Where the account is held, e.g. Wealthsimple.

month_start_day.description: The day the budget month starts on, 1 to 28.

MoneySettings.description: The ledger's own settings, carried in a backup.

path.description: An absolute path on the PC.

kind.description: `backup`: a Tally backup, which replaced the ledger.

device.description: The phone's name, shown on the PC.

replace.description: The phone's first sync with this PC: erase the PC's ledger and take the phone's.

since.description: The cursor this PC returned last time; 0 the first time.

generation.description:
The generation this PC returned last time; absent the first time. When the PC's ledger
is no longer that one, the sync is refused with `money.sync_stale`, and the phone takes
the PC's ledger whole (`since: 0`, no generation, no changes).

limit.description:
At most this many changes in the answer (1 or more). When more are left, the answer says
`more: true` and its `cursor` is where this page ended: ask again from there, and apply
the pages together once `more` is false. Absent, the whole answer at once.

MoneyChange.description:
One row's change on the sync wire (docs/MONEY.md, "Sync"). `row` holds the table's fields in
camelCase, references as uids; empty for a tombstone.

cursor.description: Store it and send it back as `since` next time.

generation.description:
Store it and send it back as `generation`: it changes when this ledger is restored,
erased or replaced, and a device holding an old one must take the ledger whole.

changes.description: This ledger's changes the device has not seen.

replaced.description: This ledger was replaced by the device's.

applied.description: The device's changes taken, and those older than what is here or not placeable.

more.description:
Only when the device asked with a `limit`: `changes` is one page and more are left. Ask
again with `since` set to `cursor` (and the same generation), and apply the pages together
once this is false. Left out when false.

Design.description:
A design canvas (`design.*`): pages of frames, shapes, text and pictures in a project,
optionally tied to one terminal. `design.get` has its nodes.

page.description: Only this page and what is on it.

nodes.description:
Pages first in their order, then every other node after its parent, siblings bottom to
top.

assets_dir.description: Where an image's `src` is, on this machine.

id.description:
Unique in the design: letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` or `:`, at most 64. Give your own
(`"hero"`, `"hero-title"`) to refer to it later in the same `design.apply`; left out,
the engine assigns one.

parent.description: The page, frame or group this node sits in. Required for everything but a page.

kind.description:
What the node is; it decides which fields it draws (see each kind). Fixed once added:
delete it and add another to change it.

name.description: Shown in the layer list and above a frame on the canvas; at most 200 characters.

x.description: Left edge in px, relative to the parent's top-left corner, within ±1000000.

y.description: Top edge in px, relative to the parent's top-left corner, within ±1000000.

w.description:
Width in px, 0 to 1000000 (`width` is read as `w`). A text with no `w` hugs its words; a
rect, ellipse, polygon or frame added without one is 100 wide, an icon 24 (within
`min_w`/`max_w`); an image needs the `w` `design.asset.add` answered; a line's follows its
points. In a laid-out frame `w_sizing` hug or fill replaces it.

h.description:
Height in px, 0 to 1000000 (`height` is read as `h`). A text hugs its lines whatever `h`
says, unless `h_sizing` is fixed; a sticky grows past it to fit its words. A shape, frame
or icon added without one gets a default as with `w`, and an image needs its `h`.

fill.description:
Background: `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`, or a `$name` colour the design names (a
`color` edit names one). Default: a frame `#FFFFFF`, a rect, ellipse or polygon
`#D9D9D9`, a sticky `#FFE58A`, a page `#1E1D1B` (the canvas colour); a text, line or path
paints none unless given one (a text's is a box behind its words, a line's or path's of
three points or more fills inside them). A text's letters are `color`.

stroke.description:
Outline colour: `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`, or a `$name` colour. A box's border
(frame, rect, sticky, image) and an ellipse's or polygon's outline are drawn only when set,
inside the edge; a line or path defaults to `#8C8C8C`; an icon is drawn in it (default: its
`color`, else dark on a light ground and light on a dark one).

stroke_width.description:
In px, 0 to 1000. Default 1 for a border or outline, 2 for a line, path or icon (an
icon's is in its 24-unit grid).

radius.description:
Corner radius of a frame, rect, sticky or image, in px (default 0; `radii` sets each
corner).

opacity.description: 0 to 1 (default 1), of the node and everything in it.

shadow.description:
A shadow under a frame, rect, ellipse, polygon, sticky or image, or with `inset` inside its
edge; a text, line, path or icon casts an outer one only, without spread (a glow when `x`
and `y` are 0). A sticky casts a soft one of its own unless given one. `x`, `y` and `spread`
within ±10000 px, `blur` 0 to 200. One shadow; `shadows` holds several (give one field or
the other).

clip.description: Whether a frame hides what overflows it (default true; a scrolling frame always does).

hidden.description:
Not drawn, not hit and left out of auto layout, with everything inside it (default
false).

locked.description:
Locked nodes cannot be selected or moved on the canvas (default false); edits still change
them.

text.description:
The words of a text or sticky, or a centred label on a rect, ellipse or polygon; at most
10000 characters. Newlines break lines.

color.description:
Colour of the letters of a text, sticky or label, and of an icon without a `stroke`:
`#RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`, or a `$name` colour (default: dark on a light ground,
light on a dark one).

font.description:
Font family of a text, sticky or label (default `Geist`; `Geist Mono` and `Sora` are
always there; `design.fonts` lists the rest). A family the desktop app lacks is drawn in
a fallback face, and the reply warns.

font_size.description: Letter size of a text, sticky or label in px, 1 to 1000 (default 16).

font_weight.description:
1 to 1000 (default 400; 600 is semibold, 700 bold); the nearest face the family has is
drawn.

italic.description: A text's or label's letters slanted (default false).

underline.description: A text's or label's letters underlined (default false).

strike.description: A line through a text's or label's letters (default false).

align.description:
A text's lines across its box: `left` (the default; `center` for a label), `center` or
`right`.

line_height.description: Line height as a multiple of the font size, 0.1 to 10 (default 1.3).

letter_spacing.description: Extra space between letters, in px, -100 to 1000 (default 0).

w_sizing.description:
Width rule (default `fixed`: its `w`; a text without a `w` hugs its words). `hug`
shrinks a text or sticky to its words and a laid-out frame to its children (nothing else
hugs); `fill` takes the room a laid-out parent leaves along its direction, or its inner
width across it.

h_sizing.description:
Height rule (default `fixed`; a text hugs its lines). A sticky's fixed `h` is a minimum
that grows to fit its words, and `hug` makes it exactly as tall as they are, as a text's
(only a text, a sticky or a frame hugs).
`fill` takes the room a laid-out parent leaves along its direction, or its inner height
across it.

layout.description:
A frame's auto layout: `row` or `column` places its children one after another, `gap`
apart inside `padding`, ignoring their `x`/`y` (an `absolute` child keeps its own); `wrap`
is a row that starts a new line when the next child would pass the frame's width. Default
`none`.

gap.description:
Space between laid-out children along a row, column or wrap line, in px, -10000 to 10000
(default 0); negative overlaps them.

padding.description:
Inner space in px, each 0 to 10000, in CSS order: `[all]`, `[vertical, horizontal]` or
`[top, right, bottom, left]`. A laid-out frame's around its children, a rect's,
ellipse's or polygon's around its label (default `[0, 12]`).

justify.description: Where a laid-out frame puts its children along its direction (default `start`).

items.description:
Where a laid-out frame puts its children across it (default `start`; `stretch` gives each
the frame's inner depth).

points.description:
A line's or path's points in px, relative to the node's `x`/`y`: at most 4000, each
within ±1000000.

arrow_start.description: A head at a line's or path's first point (default false).

arrow_end.description: A head at a line's or path's last point (default false).

src.description:
An image's picture: the `src` `design.asset.add` returned. It must be stored
(`design.asset_not_found` otherwise).

fit.description: How an image fills its box (default `cover`).

rotation.description: Clockwise turn in degrees about the node's centre, within ±3600.

sides.description: A polygon's corners, or a star's points: 3 to 24 (default 3, or 5 points for a star).

star.description:
Makes a polygon a star: its inner points at this fraction of the outer (0.05 to 0.95;
0.4 is a classic star).

radii.description: Corner radii in px, top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, instead of `radius`.

dash.description:
The stroke's dash pattern in px, 1 to 8 lengths from 0 to 1000, not all 0: `[6, 4]`
dashes, `[0, 4]` round dots. Absent is solid.

blur.description: Blur of the whole node, in px, 0 to 200.

icon.description:
An icon node's icon, one of these outline icons, drawn on a 24-unit grid scaled to the
smaller of `w` and `h` (24 is its natural size).

from.description:
A connector's start: a node on the same page, not the line itself or a page. The line
then runs from that node's edge and follows it when it moves; `points` are only where it
was last drawn.

to.description: A connector's end: a node on the same page, not the line itself or a page.

route.description: How a line runs between its ends (default `straight`).

closed.description:
Joins a line's or path's last point back to its first: a shape of your own, which
`fill` paints inside.

smooth.description: Runs a line through its `points` in a smooth curve instead of straight segments.

flip_x.description:
Mirrors a polygon, image or icon left to right. Other kinds ignore it: a line or path is
flipped by its points, a box by where it sits; text is never mirrored, and a flipped
frame's words still read left to right.

flip_y.description: Mirrors a polygon, image or icon top to bottom (other kinds as `flip_x`).

arc.description: Draws only part of an ellipse: a pie slice, a donut or an arc of a ring.

blend.description: How the node mixes with what is under it in its parent (default `normal`).

text_case.description:
Draws a text's, sticky's or label's letters upper, lower or title case; the stored words
keep theirs.

pin_x.description:
How it follows its parent's width: `left` (the default), `right`, `left_right` (its width
stretches), `center` or `scale`. Its `x`/`w` are where it sits while the parent is at its
stored `w`; a parent resized, or drawn wider or narrower (fill, stretch, hug), carries it
along. Only a child free in a frame (one without auto layout, or `absolute`) is pinned. A
stretching pin needs a fixed width (a text, a `w`); a line, path or group cannot stretch.

pin_y.description:
How it follows its parent's height: `top` (the default), `bottom`, `top_bottom` (its
height stretches), `center` or `scale`, as `pin_x` (a text needs `h_sizing: fixed` to
stretch).

absolute.description:
In a frame with auto layout: keeps its own `x`/`y` from the frame's top-left, takes no
room and is not counted when the frame hugs (a badge on a card); pin it to stick to an
edge. Elsewhere it changes nothing. Default false.

min_w.description:
Smallest width in px, 0 to 1000000, whatever decides it (hug, fill, stretch, a pin). A
fixed `w` must lie between `min_w` and `max_w`.

max_w.description:
Largest width in px, 0 to 1000000, whatever decides it; a hugging text wraps at it, and so
does a hugging `wrap` frame.

min_h.description:
Smallest height in px, 0 to 1000000, whatever decides it. A fixed `h` must lie between
`min_h` and `max_h`.

max_h.description: Largest height in px, 0 to 1000000, whatever decides it.

row_gap.description: Space between the lines of a `wrap` layout, in px, -10000 to 10000 (default: `gap`).

scroll.description:
A frame whose content scrolls that way (`x`, `y` or `both`): what overflows is clipped, a
still picture shows the start, and the canvas scrolls it with Alt+wheel. Children keep
their sizes, so a row of fixed-width cards overflows into a carousel. The scrolling axis
needs a fixed or fill size.

stroke_cap.description:
How a stroke's ends are drawn: `butt` (flat at the point), `round` or `square` (half the
weight past it). Default: `round` for a solid line or path, `butt` for dashes, `round`
for dots (`butt` would draw nothing of a dot). On a closed outline (a box, an ellipse, a
polygon) only its dashes have ends.

stroke_join.description:
How the stroke of an ellipse, polygon, line or path turns its corners: `miter` (sharp),
`round` (the default) or `bevel`.

stroke_gradient.description:
A gradient painted along the stroke instead of `stroke`'s colour, over the stroke's own
bounds (a box's border, a line's path); it draws the stroke even when `stroke` is unset.

shadows.description:
Several shadows instead of `shadow`, 1 to 8, painted in order (the last on top). A glow
is a shadow with no offset: `{"blur": 16, "color": "#4AF0FF99"}`. A text, line, path or
icon casts outer ones only, without spread. Give `shadow` or `shadows`, not both.

runs.description:
Parts of `text` styled on their own, 1 to 64, in order and not overlapping, counted in
characters (`end` not included); a field a run leaves out is the node's:
`"text": "8.4 km", "runs": [{"start": 3, "end": 6, "font_size": 14, "color": "#8C877F"}]`.
A change of `text` sends `runs` (or `null`) with it.

max_lines.description:
Most lines shown, 1 to 1000; the rest is cut and the last line shown ends in "…". The
words need a width to wrap at: a sticky, a shape's label, or a text whose width is fixed
or fills.

style.description:
A named style of the design (a `style` edit makes one; `design.get` lists them): each of
its fields this node does not set itself applies to it, so changing the style restyles
every node that names it.

motion.description:
How it moves when the design plays: 2 to 64 keys in time order on the clock of the nearest
frame or page with a `timeline` (itself included), else its page's. Its own fields are its
look at rest, which whatever does not play shows (the canvas until Play, exports,
`design.render` without `at_ms`). `dx`, `dy`, `rotate` and the scales move it from where
layout puts it; `opacity`, `fill`, `stroke`, `color`, `blur`, `sweep`, `angle` and `trim`
show their value instead of its own. Times are milliseconds:
`{"ease": "ease_out", "keys": [{"at_ms": 0, "dy": 24, "opacity": 0}, {"at_ms": 500, "dy": 0, "opacity": 1}]}`.

timeline.description:
A frame's or page's clock for the motion inside it: `{"duration_ms": 3000, "loop": true}`
(default: as long as the latest key, looping). A nested timeline keeps its own time.

width.description: `w` by another name: give one or the other.

height.description: `h` by another name: give one or the other.

DesignNode.description:
One node of a design. Every field but `kind` is optional on input; an absent style field
takes the kind's default (a white frame, a grey rect, Geist text at 16px, dark on a light
ground and light on a dark one, a yellow sticky).

oneOf.description: A sheet of the design: the root its other nodes sit in. Its `fill` is the canvas colour.

An artboard: a filled box that clips what is inside it and can lay its children out
(`layout`). Screens, cards and buttons are frames.
Nodes moved together; it paints nothing itself, and its box is its children's.
A box: `fill`, a border (`stroke`), corners (`radius`) and a centred label (`text`).
An oval filling its box (`arc` draws part of one), with a centred label (`text`).

A line through `points`, or a connector between two nodes (`from`, `to`);
`arrow_start`/`arrow_end` put heads on it.
Words (`text`), as wide as they are until given a width, then wrapped to it.
A note card: `fill` paper with `text` on it, growing to fit its words.
A freehand stroke through `points`.
A picture from `design.asset.add`, named by `src`.

A regular polygon (`sides`: 3 a triangle, 4 a diamond, 6 a hexagon…) or, with `star`, a
star of `sides` points (5 when `sides` is left out). Its first point is at the top centre.

An interface icon from Relay's set, named by `icon` (one of the names listed for `icon`),
drawn in `stroke`.

blur.description: Softness in px, 0 to 200 (default 0, a hard edge).

spread.description: How far it reaches past the edge before it blurs, in px (default 0).

inset.description: An inner shadow, cast inside the edge instead of under the node.

oneOf.description: `w`/`h` as given.

Shrink to the content: a text's or sticky's words, or a laid-out frame's children and
padding.

Stretch to the room left in a laid-out parent (along its axis; in a `wrap` layout, the
room left in its line), or to its full depth (across it).

DesignSizing.description: How a node's width or height is decided.

oneOf.description: Children keep their own `x`/`y`.
Left to right, `gap` apart.
Top to bottom, `gap` apart.

Left to right like a row, starting a new line when the next child would pass the
frame's inner width; `gap` apart along a line, `row_gap` between lines. A frame that hugs
its width wraps only at `max_w`.

DesignLayout.description: The direction a frame lays its children out in.

oneOf.description: The first at the start, the last at the end, the rest evenly between.

DesignJustify.description: Where a laid-out frame puts its children along its direction.

DesignItems.description: Where a laid-out frame puts its children across its direction.

oneOf.description: Fill the box, cropping the overflow.
Show it whole inside the box.
Stretch to the box.

DesignImageFit.description: How an image fills its box.

angle.description:
Linear: its direction in degrees as CSS reads it, 180 (the default) top to bottom, 90 left
to right. Conic: where the first stop sits, in degrees clockwise from the top (default 0).
Radial: unused.

DesignGradient.description: A gradient fill, painted instead of `fill`.

oneOf.description: From the centre out to the box's edges.

Round the centre, clockwise from `angle` (default 0, the top), as CSS
`conic-gradient(from …)`.

at.description: 0 at the start, 1 at the end.

oneOf.description: Right angles: across, then down, then across (or the other way, whichever is longer).
A smooth curve leaving and arriving along the longer axis.

DesignRoute.description: How a connector runs between its ends.

start.description: Where it starts, in degrees clockwise from the top (default 0), within ±3600.

sweep.description: How far round it goes, in degrees clockwise (default 360, the whole ellipse), within ±360.

inner.description:
The hole in the middle as a fraction of the radius, from 0 (the default, a pie) to below
1: 0.6 a donut.

cap.description:
The ends of a ring segment (`inner` above 0, `sweep` under 360): `butt` (flat, the
default), `round` (a progress ring's rounded ends) or `square`. Each end reaches half the
ring's thickness past `start` and `start + sweep`.

DesignArc.description: Part of an ellipse: a pie, a donut or a ring segment.

oneOf.description: Flat at the point.
Square, half the weight past the point.

DesignStrokeCap.description: How a stroke's ends are drawn.

DesignBlend.description: How a node mixes with what is under it in the same parent.

oneOf.description:
The first letter of each word in capitals: after a space or any punctuation (`Well-Known`,
`And/Or`), not after an apostrophe inside a word (`Don't`).

DesignTextCase.description:
How a text's letters are cased when drawn; the stored words keep theirs. Upper and lower use
Unicode's default case mapping, one letter at a time (no language's own rules).

oneOf.description: Keeps its distance from the parent's left edge (the default).
Keeps its distance from the parent's right edge.
Keeps both distances: its width stretches with the parent's.
Keeps its offset from the parent's centre line.
Keeps its place and width as fractions of the parent's width.

DesignPinX.description:
How a child follows its parent's width when the parent is resized, or drawn wider or narrower
than its stored `w`.

oneOf.description: Keeps its distance from the parent's top edge (the default).
Keeps its distance from the parent's bottom edge.
Keeps both distances: its height stretches with the parent's.
Keeps its offset from the parent's middle.
Keeps its place and height as fractions of the parent's height.

DesignPinY.description: How a child follows its parent's height, as `pin_x` does its width.

oneOf.description: Across: a carousel.
Down: a feed.

DesignScroll.description: Which way a frame's content scrolls.

oneOf.description: Sharp.
Cut off.

DesignStrokeJoin.description: How a stroke turns its corners.

end.description: The character after its last: above `start`, at most the text's length.

color.description: Its letters' colour: `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`, or a `$name` colour.

font_size.description: Its letter size in px, 1 to 1000; it also sets its line's height (`line_height` times it).

rise.description: Px above the baseline (negative below), -1000 to 1000: a superscript, a raised unit.

DesignTextRun.description:
One stretch of a text in a style of its own: characters `start` to `end` of `text` (counted
in characters, `end` not included). A field it leaves out is the node's.

keys.description: 2 to 64 keys in time order, the last at 50 ms or later.

ease.description: Ease of every move whose key names none (default `ease`).

origin.description:
The point it turns and scales about, as fractions of its box, each within ±10: `[0.5, 0.5]`
(the default) the centre, `[0.5, 1]` the bottom middle, `[0, 0]` the top left.

loop.description:
Plays its keys again from 0 every last-key ms, whatever its timeline does: spinners,
pulses (default false).

DesignMotion.description: How a node moves when its design plays.

at_ms.description: Milliseconds from the start of the timeline, 0 to 600000 (half a second is 500).

ease.description: How the move from this key to the next eases (default: the motion's `ease`).

dx.description: Moved right by this many px from where it sits (negative: left), within ±1000000.

dy.description: Moved down by this many px from where it sits (negative: up), within ±1000000.

rotate.description: Degrees clockwise added to its own rotation, about `origin`, within ±3600.

scale.description: Size multiplier about `origin`, both ways, 0 to 100 (1 as drawn).

opacity.description: 0 to 1, shown instead of its own opacity.

fill.description:
Shown instead of its fill and gradient: `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA` (a key takes no
`$name` colour).

stroke.description: Shown instead of its stroke colour: `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`.

color.description: Shown instead of its text colour: `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`.

blur.description: Layer blur in px, 0 to 200, instead of its own.

sweep.description:
An ellipse's arc sweep in degrees, -360 to 360, instead of its own (a whole ellipse sweeps
from the top): a ring that fills.

angle.description:
A linear or conic gradient's angle in degrees, within ±3600, instead of its own (and the
stroke gradient's); nothing without one.

trim.description: How much of a line's or path's stroke is drawn from its start, 0 to 1: drawing on.

DesignKey.description:
One moment of a node's motion: how it looks `at_ms` into its timeline. A key names only what
it sets; between two keys that set a property it is interpolated, before the first that sets
it the property holds that key's value, after the last that key's.

oneOf.description: CSS `ease`, cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1): the default.
cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 1, 1): departures.
cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.58, 1): arrivals.
cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1): goes a little past and settles; pops and bounces.
Holds the key's values until the next key, then jumps: blinks, frame by frame.

DesignEase.description: How a move speeds up and slows down between two keys, as CSS names them.

duration_ms.description: Its length in ms, 50 to 600000; default the latest key of the motion it clocks.

loop.description: Starts again when it ends (default true); false holds the last frame.

DesignTimeline.description: A frame's or page's clock for the motion inside it.

session.description:
The terminal it belongs to. An agent's design is its own session's; the person may
name any session of the project, or none.
Tie it to another terminal (session name), or `null` to the project alone.

title.description: Default the original's title with " copy".

ops.description:
Run in order, all or none: 1 to 2000 edits. A design holds at most 5000 nodes, 1536 KiB of
node JSON and 64 levels of nesting. A node an edit adds can be the parent of a later one.
An edit that does not read is refused by its index and the key at fault (`ops[3] update
"hero": set: …`).

base_rev.description: Refuse (`design.stale`) unless the design is still at this `rev`.

lenient.description:
Replay an undo: skip an edit of a node that no longer exists (or that this Relay cannot
read), and put back what was stored even where a new edit's rules would refuse it,
instead of refusing the whole list. Only for an `inverse` an answer gave you.

index.description: Its place among the parent's children, 0 at the bottom; absent puts it on top.

oneOf.description:
Add `node` (its `parent` is a page, frame or group already there or added earlier in
the same list).

set.description: Node fields to change, each with a value as an add takes it; null puts the field back to its default. Not id, kind or parent (move changes the parent).

oneOf.description:
Change some fields of a node: each key of `set` is a node field other than `id`, `kind`
and `parent` (use `move`); `null` puts a field back to its default.

parent.description: The new parent; absent keeps the current one.

index.description: 0 at the bottom; absent puts it on top.

keep_position.description:
Keep it where it is on the page: its `x`/`y` are rewritten for the new parent from the
stored offsets up both parents' chains. Refused (`design.position`) when it or a parent
on either side is placed by auto layout, since that place is not stored. Default false:
`x`/`y` stay as they are, relative to the new parent.

oneOf.description: Put a node in another parent, or at another place among its siblings.
Delete a node and everything inside it. A design keeps at least one page.

as.description: The copy's id; left out, the engine assigns one.

parent.description:
The page, frame or group to put the copy in; absent, the original's. A page's copy
takes none.

index.description: Its place among the parent's children, 0 at the bottom; absent puts it on top.

dx.description: Added to the copy's `x`, in px (default 0).

dy.description: Added to the copy's `y`, in px (default 0).

oneOf.description:
Copy a node and everything inside it, as one edit (a page copies as a new page). The
copy's id is `as` (left out, the engine assigns one); each node inside takes an id made
from it: one starting with the copied node's id and `-`, `_`, `.` or `:` has that start
swapped for the copy's (`card-title` becomes `card-2-title`), any other gets the copy's id
and `:` in front (`text-14` becomes `card-2:text-14`), so later edits of the same list can
name them. A connector inside joins the copies of its ends; one attached to a node outside
the copy lets go of that end, staying where it is drawn.

name.description: 1 to 64 letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` or `:`; one namespace with the styles.

oneOf.description:
Name a colour that any colour field of a node, or of a style, takes as `$name`. Naming it
again changes it wherever it is used.

name.description: 1 to 64 letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` or `:`; one namespace with the colours.

set.description: Style fields to set, each with a value as a node takes it; null takes the field out of the style.

oneOf.description:
Name a style, or change one: each key of `set` is a style field (fill, gradient, stroke,
stroke_width, dash, radius, radii, shadow, shadows, opacity, blur, blend, color, font,
font_size, font_weight, italic, underline, strike, align, line_height, letter_spacing,
text_case, stroke_cap, stroke_join, stroke_gradient) with a value as a node takes it;
`null` takes it out of the style. A node names it with `style`.

Take a named colour or style out of the design. What used it keeps its look: the colour,
or the style's fields a node did not set itself, are written into it.

DesignNodeOp.description: One edit of a design. `design.apply` runs a list of them in order, all or none.

prev_rev.description:
The `rev` before these edits: when it is not the one you last read, someone else
changed the design in between; read it again with `design.get`.

nodes.description: Each node an edit added, changed or moved, as stored now.

removed.description: The ids deleted, with everything that was inside them.

ids.description:
For each edit, the id of the node it acted on (an `add`'s assigned id); empty for one
skipped by `lenient`.

inverse.description: The edits that undo these, in the order to apply them.

warnings.description:
For an agent, what a lenient list applied as written although a strict one would have
refused it, or skipped because this Relay cannot read the node: each edit's label and
why (at most 20).

path.description: A PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG file on this machine, copied in.

bytes_b64.description: The picture itself, base64, instead of `path` (at most 1 MiB decoded).

w.description: Its natural size in px (an SVG's declared size, or 300 by 150).
